title: Situated Inference: Adapting Frozen Generative Speech Enhancement under Acoustic Distribution Shift
tldr: Situated Inference adapts a frozen generative speech enhancer to a new acoustic environment by changing how it is run, not what it has learned. From a small set of paired target speech it selects the observation processing, the reverse starting point, and the solver step count, then keeps that strategy fixed for subsequent inputs.
abstract: Diffusion and flow matching models typically enhance speech using fixed inference strategies that may become unsuitable under acoustic distribution shifts in real-world deployment. Our cross-condition analysis shows that the advantage of an inference strategy is not consistently preserved across acoustic conditions, even when the model weights and solver update rule remain fixed. This finding motivates Situated Inference, which specializes a frozen generative enhancer to a target acoustic distribution through its inference strategy. Situated Inference evaluates a structured inference space that jointly varies observation processing, the reverse starting point, and the solver step count, thereby constructing a target-specific quality and computation profile. From this profile, it selects one strategy either to maximize enhancement quality or to minimize computation subject to the reference quality, then fixes that strategy for subsequent inputs. Across four generative backbones and three acoustic conditions, Situated Inference improves perceptual speech quality under quality specialization and reduces the number of function evaluations under efficiency specialization. Deployment on the Ameca humanoid further demonstrates the practical effectiveness of Situated Inference under real-world acoustic conditions.

robot.title: Situated Inference on the Ameca humanoid
text: Each trial is recorded in a real room. A loudspeaker plays a noisy utterance from the LSM condition and Ameca listens through its own ear microphone, which is the Ameca heard recording. The frozen backbone’s measured inference time for that utterance, on an NVIDIA H200 at batch size 1, is reproduced as a pause, after which Ameca speaks the enhanced output with lip-sync. Each clip is uncut, so the visible wait is exactly the reproduced compute time.

Every row races the backbone’s default strategy against the strategies selected by Situated Inference under the quality and efficiency objectives on one shared time axis. For SGMSE+ and StoRM the two objectives select the same strategy.
robot.howto: Play all runs the three arms in sync with the sound of the fastest arm. Click a video while it plays to listen to that arm instead, or use its play button to watch it alone.
